citation: Monro J, Mishra S, Stoklosinski H et al. (2022). Dietary Fibre and Organic Acids in Kiwifruit Suppress Glycaemic Response Equally by Delaying Absorption—A Randomised Crossover Human Trial with Parallel Analysis of 13C-Acetate Uptake. Nutrients 14(15):3189.
protocol: Five breakfasts, randomised crossover, each 30 g Weet-Bix (~20 g carbohydrate) plus: kiwifruit sugars only (20.4 g glucose:fructose:sucrose 2:2:1), 200 g whole kiwifruit, neutralised kiwifruit, kiwifruit juice, or sugars + organic acids. Capillary blood at -5, 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min.
population: n=9 healthy adults (6 women, 3 men), aged 18-40, BMI 25.9 ± 4.5 (20.6-32.9) kg/m2, no diabetes (Table A1).

reports.where: Table 2: incremental peak, iAUC30, iAUC180 per meal
Table 3: peak height, iAUC30, iAUC180 per meal, µU/mL·min, mean and SEM columns

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: cereal + kiwifruit sugars vs cereal + whole kiwifruit (same sugars plus fruit fibre); the juice arm splits fibre from acids. Isolates fruit fibre at fixed sugars with juice and acid controls. Watch: organic acids and pH are confounders the model cannot see (use the sugars vs whole fruit and juice vs whole fruit pairs), capillary glucose, n=9. Only in figures: time courses.
